720	The head knows what is right and what is wrong.
721	Right? For example, a person about to commit a sin
722	usually knows he is about to commit a sin. That is why
723	he looks right and left. Why? Because the mind
724	knows it is not good. But why does he commit
725	the sin? Because the heart craves. The heart has desire.
726	So if you are a king, the mind rules the heart, then the mind
727	defeats the heart. If you are a Lemech, first craving,
728	and only afterward the intellect, then you are like the nations. So what does He
729	say to him? "And He will give their kings into your hand": whatever you call
730	their way, which is the way of Lemech, will be yours,
731	you will rule over it. Another point:
732	Why does He give the kings? So that you know that if
733	the king falls,
734	the whole people falls after him. Right? How would He make
735	their minister in heaven fall? The moment Moshe Rabbeinu saw the minister
736	of Og thrown down to the floor, he understood that they were already
737	losing. The moment the one in heaven is cast to the ground, the whole
738	people will lose. Same thing here on earth. The people see the
739	king fall, they all surrender and do not fight. How
740	do we know? In Yehoshua it is written: "And they brought out those kings
741	to Yehoshua." They won, they brought the kings
742	to Yehoshua. "And Yehoshua called all the men of Israel and said
743	to the commanders of the men of war who went with him: Come near, put your
744	feet upon the necks of these kings." They made the
745	kings lie down, and all the commanders of Israel put their
746	foot on their necks, which is the sign of humiliation and submission,
747	and it was fulfilled exactly as written here: "And He will give their kings
748	into your hand." Exactly. You see, He promised here, and it indeed
749	happened.
750	What does He say now? He says: "The graven images of their gods
751	you shall burn with fire; you shall not covet the silver or gold upon them
752	and take it for yourself." Why? "Lest you be snared by it, for it is an abomination to
753	HaShem your Elokim." That is, you arrive and conquer
754	their village, and there is plunder. Part of what they had was
755	idols of idol worship. Now, what would they do?
756	The idol, they would make perhaps of wood
757	or stone, but adorn it with gold jewelry.
758	So He says: first of all, burn their idols,
759	but what about the silver and gold? What a pity, there is silver and gold.
760	Well, we could melt it down, maybe make rings
761	and bracelets for a woman, something. HaKadosh Baruch Hu says: do not
762	covet silver and gold upon them. What is on the idols too,
763	burn, destroy. Why? "Lest you be snared by it," like a land mine. Even
764	if you melt it down, it will always nag at the back of your mind that it was once
765	idol worship, and perhaps in the end it will make you fall
766	and you will serve it somehow. So He says "lest you be snared": you do not know.
767	You say, "No, I am strong." You cannot be
768	strong, you do not know. There once was an inclination
769	for idol worship, just as a man is forbidden to be secluded with
770	a woman who is not his wife, in what is called yichud,
771	you do not know. Do not say "I am strong." There is no
772	guardian for lions, the Sages say. You do not know
773	how it will make you fall. Same with idol worship.
774	The Sages abolished the inclination for idol worship. Today we do not
775	understand this, but once there was a very strong inclination
776	for idol worship. So He says you do not know
777	how it will make you fall, what is called
778	a trap. Why? "For it is an abomination to HaShem your Elokim."
779	"And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, lest you become a devoted thing
780	like it. You shall utterly detest it and utterly abhor it, for it is a devoted thing."
781	What does it say? Do not bring an abomination into your house, and do not bring
782	anything connected with idol worship into the house. Where is this relevant
783	today? There are poor people who do not know,
784	they come back from the East, they bring statues of this, Buddha,
785	what is he called? They bring statues of idol
786	worship like that. They put them in the house as decoration. All kinds of
787	things used in idol worship in the Far East, they put
788	these statues of this Buddha, and they think
789	it is decoration, but it is idol worship.
790	"Do not bring idol worship into your house." So wait, a person
791	will say, what is the problem? Do I bow to it? Do I
792	worship it? It is just decoration. Tell me, if now
793	the police come to someone's house, do a search, and find
794	there a machine for printing dollars,
795	he says, "But I did not print dollars for myself, I only
796	keep the machine." Ah, they will say, fine, then you are
797	fine, you are great? Of course not! Or a lab,
798	equipment for producing drugs, he says, "But I did not
799	produce drugs." But sir, you have prohibited equipment here.
800	So you see, even if you did not commit
801	the crime, the very fact that you keep the tools for committing
802	the crime, you will also be held to account for that in court. Right?
803	Same thing: you bring idol worship home, you
804	say, "But I did not worship it." So what is it doing in your
805	house? So whoever does not know, poor thing, that is why
806	we listen to a Torah class. It is worth it for everyone to go through the house,
807	look whether he has anything resembling idol worship, all kinds of
808	statues, all kinds of unrelated things, throw them out of the
809	house. Why do you need it? On the Day of Judgment,
810	you will give an account for such a thing. May HaShem have mercy. Some
811	say "Do not bring an abomination into your house" refers to the
812	beautiful woman, that if you go to war and see a beautiful
813	gentile woman, even though the Torah, under very, very,
814	very, very parallel conditions, permitted her to you,
815	they say "do not bring an abomination into your house."
816	Now, what else is "do not bring an abomination into your house
817	and you shall be a devoted thing like it"? Cherem is the letters of chomer,
818	right, without the vav, so that you not be far from HaShem, with a spirit of
819	materialism without spirituality. For what is cherem? Cherem is
820	matter. Matter distances you from HaShem. Cherem is also
821	the letters of Ramach, that if you bring an abomination it will bring
822	troubles on your 248 limbs. Cherev, sword, is also the letters of rachem,
823	for whoever repents and, as it were, throws it out
824	of the house, HaShem has mercy on him. So you see how many
825	hints. Now, what else does He say to him? "All the commandment which
826	I command you this day you shall observe to do, that you may live,
827	and multiply, and go in and possess the land which HaShem swore
828	to your fathers." That is, what does He say to him?
829	"That you may live and multiply." That is, see, the Torah
830	is a Torah of life, and HaKadosh Baruch Hu promises
831	that fulfilling the mitzvot brings a person vitality. Wait, but
832	someone will say, wait, I know some who
833	keep nothing, and they live. I know one who transgresses
834	every sin, eats pork, eats this,
835	desecrates Shabbat, and lives, right? He lives physically like
836	a cow, like a dog, a dog also lives, a cow also lives. But
837	what? They live physically, but he has no spiritual
838	vitality. Vitality is a spiritual matter, and it continues
839	afterward to the World to Come. Woe to whoever comes
